title: A Calligraphy Pen and Ink
description: Explore decorative handwriting through a pen’s split tip, flowing ink, and the shapes of a letter.
cardDescription: Explore decorative handwriting through a pen’s split tip, flowing ink, and the shapes of a letter.
focus: Calligraphy uses controlled strokes to form letters. The clues distinguish the tool’s point from the line it makes and the small marks within a letterform.
solvingTip: Use a physical pen part or a simple stroke shape before trying the lettering terms.
words: Pointed writing part of a dip or fountain pen
One of the two sides of a split pen tip
Small finishing projection on the end of some letter strokes
One drawn line or movement forming part of a letter
Angle at which a written letter leans
Colored liquid used in a calligraphy pen
Hand-held writing tool fitted with a point
Decorative curved flourish at a letter's end
Enclosed curved form within a written letter
Straight or curved mark made by the pen
Narrow cut separating a nib's two sides
To lower a pen point into its ink supply
Light reference line helping align the letters

answerNotes.NIB: A nib holds and delivers ink; it is separate from the handle supporting it.
answerNotes.TINE: Tines are divided by a slit; their shape and flexibility affect how a nib writes.
answerNotes.SERIF: A serif is a letterform feature, not a required feature of every calligraphic style.
answerNotes.STROKE: A stroke is one component of a letter; several may combine to make the finished character.
answerNotes.SLANT: Slant describes orientation, while line thickness describes another aspect of the writing.

title: Binding a Small Handmade Book
description: Look at the folds, sewing, and cover parts used to assemble a small handmade book.
cardDescription: Look at the folds, sewing, and cover parts used to assemble a small handmade book.
focus: A book’s sheets can be folded into sections before they are sewn or attached. The clues distinguish those groups from the cover, spine, and materials joining them.
solvingTip: Separate the paper structure from the protective cover and the fastening materials.
words: Construction joining a book's pages and cover
Group of folded sheets forming a section of a book
Sheet joining or lining the inside of a book's cover
Back edge of a book where its pages are joined
Pointed tool used to make sewing holes in folded paper
To bend a sheet over to form a booklet section
Strand used to sew a handmade book
Tool carrying thread through the sewing holes
Adhesive joining parts of a book
Protective outer layer around the pages
Single sheet within a book, having two page sides
Device holding the book firmly during binding work
Fabric covering used on many book boards
Outer boundary of the trimmed page block

answerNotes.BINDING: Binding names the assembly or its structure, not the written text inside the book.
answerNotes.SIGNATURE: Signature has a bookmaking meaning here, different from an author's handwritten name.
answerNotes.ENDPAPER: Endpapers connect or finish the cover area; they are distinct from the main printed pages.
answerNotes.SPINE: The spine is the bound edge rather than the front or back cover panel.
answerNotes.AWL: An awl pierces a hole; the needle and thread form the later sewn connection.

title: A Linocut Print on the Table
description: Explore a relief print through its carved block, roller, and the paper receiving the inked image.
cardDescription: Explore a relief print through its carved block, roller, and the paper receiving the inked image.
subtheme: A Linocut Print on the Table
focus: A linocut prints from the raised surface left after carving. Cut-away areas generally do not receive the same ink, which distinguishes relief printing from an engraved recessed line.
solvingTip: Identify what is carved away and what remains high enough to print.
words: Relief print made from a carved linoleum block
Small hand roller spreading ink over a printing block
Curved or angled cutting tool used to remove a channel
Printing method in which raised areas transfer the image
Trial impression used to inspect a developing print
Colored material rolled onto the raised block surface
Carved plate carrying a relief image
To remove a portion of the linoleum surface
To move the inking tool across the block
To apply force transferring the image to the sheet
Picture or design transferred from the carved surface
Outer boundary of the printing block
Shallow surface used to spread printing ink

answerNotes.LINOCUT: Linocut uses linoleum rather than a wood block; the raised surface carries the image ink.
answerNotes.BRAYER: A brayer distributes ink; it is different from the tool removing material from the block.
answerNotes.GOUGE: A gouge cuts recessed areas, leaving other areas raised to carry ink.
answerNotes.RELIEF: Relief prints from the upper surface rather than from ink-filled recessed grooves.
answerNotes.PROOF: A proof lets a maker assess the image before the final edition.

title: Swirls in a Marbled Paper Sheet
description: Follow decorative paper marbling through floating colors, a combed pattern, and the sheet lifted from a bath.
cardDescription: Follow decorative paper marbling through floating colors, a combed pattern, and the sheet lifted from a bath.
subtheme: Swirls in a Marbled Paper Sheet
focus: In a familiar marbling method, colors float on a prepared bath and transfer to paper. The clues distinguish the liquid surface from the sheet receiving its pattern.
solvingTip: Use the material’s state and position: floating color, supporting liquid, or lifted sheet.
words: Paper-decorating technique producing swirling stone-like patterns
Thickened liquid bath supporting colors in one paper-marbling method
Row of points drawn through floating color to form a pattern
Spiraling curve in a marbled paper design
Single flat piece of paper lifted from the marbling bath
Shallow container holding the marbling bath
Small amount of color placed on the liquid surface
Colored fluid used in some marbling techniques
Material carrying the finished decorative pattern
Thin branching line suggesting a natural stone pattern
To remain supported at a liquid surface
To draw a pointed tool through the floating colors
Body of liquid on which the pattern is prepared
To raise the decorated sheet away from the liquid

answerNotes.MARBLING: Marbling transfers a surface pattern onto paper; methods and bath preparations vary among traditions.
answerNotes.SIZE: Size has a craft meaning here; other marbling traditions use different liquid arrangements.
answerNotes.COMB: A marbling comb organizes the color on the bath; it is not a hair-care tool in this scene.
answerNotes.SWIRL: A swirl describes the visual shape, not a particular paint ingredient.
answerNotes.SHEET: The sheet receives the pattern; it is separate from the liquid supporting the colors.

title: Printing a Card at an Old-Time Press
description: Visit a small printing press through its ink, paper, letters, and a freshly made card.
cardDescription: Visit a small printing press through its ink, paper, letters, and a freshly made card.
subtheme: Printing a Card at an Old-Time Press
focus: The press puts inked letters onto paper. These clues focus on the printed message and familiar materials.
solvingTip: Try a short writing or color word first.
words: Machine that puts inked letters onto paper
Colored printing material placed on the letters
Letters arranged for printing on an old press
Thin sheet receiving the printed message
Small stiff sheet printed with a greeting
One alphabet character in the printed message
Group of letters forming part of the greeting
One printed side of a sheet
Make a copy of words or a design with ink
Turn a cylinder over an inked surface
Shallow holder keeping printing materials together
No longer wet, as ink must be before handling
Dark ink color used for a clear printed message

answerNotes.PRESS: A printing press uses pressure to transfer the inked design to a sheet.
answerNotes.INK: Ink carries the printed image from the type to the paper.
answerNotes.TYPE: Type refers to the printable letter pieces in this scene.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper is the receiving surface, rather than the ink applied to it.
answerNotes.CARD: A greeting card is one possible product of a small printing press.
